one_line_contribution: A head-to-head test of whether a cheap 10-dimensional judge-derived failure-mode signature predicts source-to-target warm-start gain for *textual* reflective prompt optimization better than SPoT-style semantic/task-embedding similarity, with the transfer matrix's split-half reliability measured first as an explicit ceiling on any predictor and an abstaining leave-one-target-out router as the payoff.
closest_prior_work: Two clusters. (1) SPoT/ATTEMPT and Vu et al. 2020, which the proposal handles correctly: they predict transfer from task embeddings for soft prompts/fine-tuning, and the proposal's claim is a feature-space claim rather than the text-instead-of-soft-prompts domain swap the brief warns about, so these do not sink it. (2) The one that actually threatens it and is never cited: intermediate-task transfer source selection — Pruksachatkun et al. 2020, Poth et al. 2021 ('What to Pre-Train on? Efficient Intermediate Task Selection'), and especially TaskWeb/TaskShop (Kim et al. 2023), which builds a measured source x target transfer matrix over many tasks and uses it to *select* a source, including cheap proxy-score selection. That literature already establishes (a) transfer matrices are worth measuring, (b) semantic/embedding similarity is a mediocre selector, and (c) a cheap proxy score on the target is a strong selector — which is exactly this proposal's predictor (d). Against that backdrop the delta narrows to 'failure signatures are the right feature space, and the setting is reflective text-prompt search', which is real but thinner than the Related Work section implies, and the proposal's own risk factor (4) concedes the contribution collapses if predictor (d) wins.
strongest_objection: The headline claims are stated at a resolution the design's own unit of generalization cannot resolve. The proposal correctly declares that the bootstrap is clustered on target task 'the unit of generalization' — and there are 8 targets. The power calculation offered (Spearman 0.27 at 80% with 56 cells) is for a single unclustered correlation and does not license Falsifiable Prediction (b), which is a *difference between two dependent correlations* of >=0.2 under target-clustered resampling over 8 clusters; that comparison will not have a CI excluding zero except by luck. Prediction (c) is worse: leave-one-target-out gives 8 router decisions, so the '<=5% vs ~25% negative-transfer incidents' claim rests on roughly 1 versus 6 events out of 24 target-seed cells, whose binomial intervals overlap almost completely, and '>=60% of oracle-minus-cold-start gain' is a ratio of two noisy quantities estimated from 8 held-out targets. This is precisely failure mode 2 the research brief told proposals to avoid. Two secondary objections compound it: (i) the headline Spearman is computed over all 56 cells, so it is inflated or masked by target main effects — the proposal knows this (it includes an additive source+target baseline) but predictions (b) and (d) are stated on raw, not residualized, Delta, and the quantity a router actually needs is the *within-target* ranking of sources, which is 7 items per row; (ii) Delta is pooled across tasks with non-commensurate metrics (MBPP pass rate, GSM8K exact match, HotpotQA F1, instruction-following), so 'test points' are not a common currency and the '6 test points spread' in prediction (a) is not well defined across rows. Third, a conceptual gap in the construct: the failure signature is measured from a *fixed baseline/seed* prompt's failures (step 5), but the artifact being transferred is the *optimized, domain-scrubbed* source prompt, whose residual failure profile is by construction different from the baseline's — the feature describes the task-under-a-bad-prompt while the treatment is a good prompt, and no experiment tests that the signature of the optimized source predicts anything.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Buy statistical resolution instead of breadth of analysis: raise the task count to ~14-16 clusters (cheap, since cells are 50-rollout runs and BBH/SNI supply many clusters) so the router has enough leave-one-target-out folds to support prediction (c), or else demote (c) from a claim to a descriptive figure and make the reliability-plus-predictor comparison the paper. (2) State predictions (b) and (d) on target-residualized Delta and report the within-target rank correlation (mean Spearman across 8 rows of 7) as the primary quantity, since that is what routing consumes; convert Delta to a per-task standardized effect (divide by the step-1 per-task metric SD) before pooling. (3) Pre-register the difference-of-dependent-correlations test with its own power analysis under target-clustered resampling, and report the minimum detectable correlation *gap*, not the minimum detectable correlation. (4) Add the signature of the optimized source prompt (and of the source's residual failures after optimization) as a predictor variant, since that is the object actually being transferred. (5) Resolve the internal inconsistency in Measurement and Noise Control: 'the reflection proposal stream is replayed to remove proposal randomness' is not achievable in the warm-start arm, whose whole treatment is that reflection sees a different starting prompt — say plainly that replay applies only to the null replicate and the re-scoring study. (6) Say explicitly whether the 56-cell matrix is run on both Qwen2.5-7B and 32B or only one; the experiment section reads as both, which roughly doubles the compute and is the only place the budget looks unsafe.
missing_baseline: A placebo warm start: a well-formed, domain-general instruction skeleton that was never optimized on any source task (role framing + output contract + decomposition + error-avoidance clauses, hand-written or LLM-written to match the scrubbed sources in length and register). Random-source controls for *which* source, but every arm in the plan starts from an optimized artifact, so nothing in the design separates 'transfer of optimization signal' from 'any competent generic prompt beats GEPA's cold seed at 50 rollouts' — and step 8's own finding that gains may be mostly output-format compliance makes that the likely explanation. Secondary omissions a reviewer would also press: (i) a multi-source arm (merge or concatenate the 7 scrubbed sources, or best-of-k warm starts under the same rollout budget), which is the obvious competitor to routing and may beat it outright; (ii) a budget-amortized cold start — warm start at 50 rollouts silently consumes the 300 rollouts spent optimizing the source, so a cold-start arm given a matched *total* budget should be reported alongside the 50-rollout pairing, even if the amortization argument (source cost paid once, reused 7 times) is the one the paper defends.
preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty. Judged on what the text provides, no preprint search was performed and none is reported anywhere else in the submission: the Related Work names GEPA (2025) and MIPROv2 (2024) but engages only with indexed 2020-2021 soft-prompt transfer work, and its central novelty claim — that no one has measured a reliability-quantified source x target matrix for textual optimized prompts or tested failure-signature versus semantic predictors — is asserted, not searched. That is a weakness, not a neutral, and in this area it is a live risk: warm-starting and prompt-library reuse are the most obvious follow-ups to a 2025 optimizer, GEPA-style systems already ship reusable prompt artifacts, and automatic discovery of domain-general LLM failure taxonomies (rather than the hand-specified 10 modes here) has been an active 2025 preprint topic; any of these could already contain the transfer matrix or the taxonomy-as-feature idea. I cannot name a specific colliding arXiv entry from the submission alone, and establishing that was the authors' burden. Note also that the closest *indexed* threat — TaskWeb/TaskShop and the intermediate-task-selection line — was missed even without a preprint search, which lowers confidence that a search would have been thorough.
